etymologies.etymologyHTML: From cow +‎ boy. More on Wikipedia.

definitions.definition: A man who tends free-range cattle, especially in the American West.

quote.citation: 1899, Stephen Crane, chapter 1, in Twelve O'Clock:
quote.text: There was some laughter, and Roddle was left free to expand his ideas on the periodic visits of cowboys to the town. “Mason Rickets, he had ten big punkins a-sittin' in front of his store, an' them fellers from the Upside-down-F ranch shot 'em up […].”

definitions.definition: A man who identifies with cowboy culture, including wearing a cowboy hat and being a fan of country and western music.
(informal) A person who engages in reckless behavior, especially for the purpose of showing off.
(British, informal) A dishonest or incompetent independent tradesman.
(card games, slang) A playing card of king rank.
(intransitive) To work as a cowboy, herding cattle.

quote.citation: 1994, Sherry Robinson, El Malpais, Mt. Taylor, and the Zuni Mountains: a hiking guide and history:
quote.text: Besides cowboying he worked at a small sawmill that cut logs into "four slabs and a tie" and sold ties to the railroad.
Derwood Bailey cowboyed for 50 cents a day, a noon meal, and a gallon of oats for his horse.

quote.citation: 2003, C. J. Hadley, Trappings of the Great Basin Buckaroo:
quote.text: I still had never ridden or cowboyed, and I wanted to learn something about it. I'd been making the damn saddles for years but didn't know how to use them.
